text:
anya: Heads up — after switching the q6b-lite int4 profile on newmodel-v2 for throughput testing, our paraphrase promptset shows a clear collapse. Perf numbers: +2.3x tokens/sec but BLEU-like metric down ~18% on paraphrase anchors. Samples: s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase-bank/v3b/fail-sample-ids.txt :frowning:

tom: Ugh. Do we know if it's a tokenization mismatch or the quant kernel? Any diffs in tokenizer version between the eval runner and model build?

anya: Tokenizer versions match (v2.1), but I noticed a lot of near-duplicates in the failing set that look like tokenwalk shuffles (short paraphrases collapsing to same sequence). Attaching quick sample: 

devin: Can you drop the sample ids here? I can re-run the eval with debug KV traces. If the KV cache homogeneity is the problem we'll see identical cached prefixes.

anya: pasted 10 example pairs inline (ids 98312,98317,...). Many show short-prefix overlap. Also ran a quick local dedupe with threshold 0.86 and got 9% overlap reduction.

marta: @anya @devin we can prioritize a labeler micro-batch for these edge paraphrases. We have capacity for 600 judgments/day if we limit context to 2-turn summary + anchor. How fast do you need relabeled anchors?

lex: Propose a two-track triage: (1) rerun eval with kernel fallback (float16) to confirm quant impact, (2) expand paraphrase anchors and do a targeted relabel on the dedup-reduced set. If float16 removes the regression it's kernel/quant; else it's dataset/anchor coverage.

devin: Running the kernel fallback now. Command I used: 
```
./eval_run --model newmodel-v2:q6b-lite --prompts s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase-bank/v3b/manifest.json \ 
  --debug-kv --fallback-kernel float16 --out ./runs/newmodel-v2-q6b-debug.json
```

labelops_bot: Label queue created: queue_id=lab-q-2026-03-23-77, size=842, sampler=paraphrase-dedupe-0.86, priority=high

marta: Got the queue id. We'll split into 4 labeler shards (210 each). ETA first shard tomorrow EOD PST. I'll add an instruction doc for short-context labeling and mark uncertain = "needs review" so we can escalate tricky paraphrase merges.

anya: Thanks. Action items so far: 1) @devin rerun with float16 fallback and share diff (priority) — assigned. 2) @marta spin labeler shards and push anchors to golden review — assigned. 3) I'll run tokenwalk dedupe with adaptive threshold and surface a curated candidate list. Command I'm going to run: 
```
tokenwalk dedupe --input s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase-bank/v3b/manifest.json \ 
  --out s3://redwood-curation/paraphrase-bank/v3b/dedup-0.84.json --threshold 0.84 --keep-anchors 5000
```

tom: Also add a quick metric: fraction_of_identical_first_8_tokens between paraphrase pairs — if that spikes post-quant that's a smoking gun. Can we log that in the eval_run?

devin: float16 fallback run finished — diff looks like: paraphrase BLEU drop disappears (now within 2% of baseline). Uploading trace: s3://redwood-runs/newmodel-v2/q6b-debug-6790012345.json. Initial read shows repeated cached prefixes for many failing ids.

anya: Good catch — looks like quant kernel causes prefix normalization on some token encodings. Next: try a small kernel tweak (disable prefix-normalization scalar) and rebench. lex, can you coordinate with runtime team for a quick kernel flag?

lex: Looping in runtime infra. I'll open a runtime issue and request a canary build with flag `--preserve-prefix-encodings`. If the canary matches float16, we can ship a patch; else we proceed with dataset relabel + anchor expansion as fallback.

marta: Labelers prepped. Starting first shard now. I'll post daily progress updates here and ping when the first 210 are done. :thumbsup:

anya: Perf vs quality tradeoff notes will go into the rollout doc. For now, block the q6b-lite profile from auto-rollout until we confirm kernel patch or complete anchor relabel and regression recheck.

tom: Agreed. Also let's add a small synthetic paraphrase augment to the golden anchors to cover the short-prefix collapse cases (e.g., small edit distance swaps). I'll prototype 200 synthetic anchors and drop them into the review queue.

labelops_bot: Queue update: shard1=210 assigned, shard2..4 pending. Progress URL: https://labels.redwood/queues/lab-q-2026-03-23-77

anya: Thank you all — next status in ~24hrs unless someone hits an unblock sooner.
